# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

## PR Description

### What changed
Confluence storage→Markdown now handles `ac:adf-node` explicitly (parity with Java dm.ai #596 / PR epam/dm.ai#618): synced blocks (`type="bodied-sync-block"`) render their `<ac:adf-content>` payload inline through the normal converters, while real extensions (draw.io / ecosystem apps) emit the `[Diagram]` placeholder instead of leaking attribute GUID text.

### Key decisions
- Added `_wrapAdfNode` to the `_wrapStorage` dispatch chain (structural parser, so no regex pre-pass like Java's); missing `ac:adf-content` falls back to rendered children, mirroring Java's defensive fallback.
- Split `confluence_markdown.dart` (was 805 lines, over the 800 loc gate) into a `part` file `confluence_markdown_storage.dart` for the storage→Markdown half — repo's existing `part` convention (cf. `jira_client.dart`), zero public API change.
- New `confluence_synced_block_markdown_test.dart` mirrors the Java `ConfluenceSyncedBlockMarkdownTest` (paragraph + code macro survive inline, table converts, no GUID leakage, extension → `[Diagram]`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/
crap4dart check --all   # loc gate back under 800; coverage 96.6%
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  N[ac:adf-node] --> T{type attr}
  T -->|bodied-sync-block| C[ac:adf-content] --> P[render inline via existing converters]

# gh-306: Confluence storage→Markdown: adf-node parity — synced blocks inline, real extensions as [Diagram] (Java #596 / PR epam/dm.ai#618)

## Description

## Parity with the Java DMtools (dm.ai) `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown`

Java issue https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/596 fixed a content-loss bug: `<ac:adf-node>` was blanket-replaced with `[Diagram]`, which silently dropped **synced blocks** (`type="bodied-sync-block"`) that carry their real content inline in `<ac:adf-content>`. Fixed by PR https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/pull/618 (merged).

## Dart status today (verified, not a bug — but not parity either)

The Dart port (`lib/src/integrations/confluence/confluence_markdown.dart`) uses a **structural XML parser** (`_parseXml` → `_storageNodeToMarkdown` → `_wrapStorage`), not the Java regex pipeline. Unknown tags fall through `_wrapInlineStyle`'s default branch which returns children **verbatim**. Consequences:

- ✅ **Synced blocks do NOT lose content** — `ac:adf-extension` / `ac:adf-node` / `ac:adf-content` are all "unknown" and pass their children through, so a `bodied-sync-block`'s inner paragraphs/code/tables survive. The #596 bug does **not** reproduce in Dart.
- ❌ **No `[Diagram]` placeholder for real extensions** — a draw.io/ecosystem extension (`ac:adf-node type="extension"`) currently renders its `ac:adf-attribute` children (extension-key, resource-id GUIDs) as verbatim text noise instead of the clean `[Diagram]` placeholder Java emits.
- ❌ Behavior is **implicit** (relies on the unknown-tag passthrough) and **untested** for both synced blocks and extensions.

## Scope (parity with Java #596)
1. Handle `ac:adf-node` explicitly in `_wrapStorage` (or the block dispatch):
   - `type="bodied-sync-block"` → render the inner `ac:adf-content` content inline (paragraphs, code macros, tables via the existing converters). Today this works by accident via passthrough — make it explicit and lock it with a test.
   - `type="extension"` (draw.io, ecosystem apps — no readable content) → emit the `[Diagram]` placeholder, matching Java.
2. Unit tests in the Dart mirror of the Java `ConfluenceSyncedBlockMarkdownTest`: synced-block paragraph + code macro survive inline (no `[Diagram]`), and a real draw.io extension maps to `[Diagram]` with no attribute GUID leakage.

## Acceptance criteria
- Synced-block content converts inline (same as Java's fixed output).
- Real extensions produce the `[Diagram]` placeholder (Java parity).
- New unit tests cover both cases; existing converter tests stay green.

_Do not assign / implement here — this is a parity tracking issue._

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Java uses a lazy regex `(.*?)` with `Pattern.DOTALL` — for NESTED adf-nodes, the lazy match would stop at the FIRST `</ac:adf-node>`, so nested structures break in Java (regex can't nest). Dart's structural parser handles nesting correctly. That's an improvement, not a regression.

# dart_test.yaml — configuration for the `dart test` runner.
#
# Test layers (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy, and
# test/integration/README.md):
#
#   L1 unit     — test/**, everything mocked. Default run + CI quality.yml.
#   L2 contract — recorded Java tool traffic replayed against Dart clients.
#   L3 live     — real APIs against sandbox instances; tagged `integration`.
#   L4 agents   — dmtools-agents suite under the Dart runtime (own CI job).
#
# The L3 layer is EXCLUDED from the default run so live-API tests never slow
# down or destabilize the quality loop:
#
#   dart test                                # L1 + L2; the L3 suite is skipped
#
# The `integration` preset opts back in. The default skip is sticky, so
# `-t integration` alone still skips the tag — the preset is what re-enables
# it:
#
#   dart test -P integration -t integration  # L3 only; real credentials needed
#
# CI runs L3 nightly and via workflow_dispatch
# (.github/workflows/integration.yml), never per-PR by default.

tags:
  integration:
    skip: >-
      Live integration test — excluded from the default run. Target a sandbox
      via the DMTOOLS_IT_* variables and run explicitly with
      `dart test -P integration -t integration`.

presets:
  # Re-enables the `integration` tag so the L3 suite can run on demand.
  integration:
    tags:
      integration:
        skip: false

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

## PR Description

### What changed
Confluence storage→Markdown now handles `ac:adf-node` explicitly (parity with Java dm.ai #596 / PR epam/dm.ai#618): synced blocks (`type="bodied-sync-block"`) render their `<ac:adf-content>` payload inline through the normal converters, while real extensions (draw.io / ecosystem apps) emit the `[Diagram]` placeholder instead of leaking attribute GUID text.

### Key decisions
- Added `_wrapAdfNode` to the `_wrapStorage` dispatch chain (structural parser, so no regex pre-pass like Java's); missing `ac:adf-content` falls back to rendered children, mirroring Java's defensive fallback.
- Split `confluence_markdown.dart` (was 805 lines, over the 800 loc gate) into a `part` file `confluence_markdown_storage.dart` for the storage→Markdown half — repo's existing `part` convention (cf. `jira_client.dart`), zero public API change.
- New `confluence_synced_block_markdown_test.dart` mirrors the Java `ConfluenceSyncedBlockMarkdownTest` (paragraph + code macro survive inline, table converts, no GUID leakage, extension → `[Diagram]`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/
crap4dart check --all   # loc gate back under 800; coverage 96.6%
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD

# gh-306: Confluence storage→Markdown: adf-node parity — synced blocks inline, real extensions as [Diagram] (Java #596 / PR epam/dm.ai#618)

## Description

## Parity with the Java DMtools (dm.ai) `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown`

Java issue https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/596 fixed a content-loss bug: `<ac:adf-node>` was blanket-replaced with `[Diagram]`, which silently dropped **synced blocks** (`type="bodied-sync-block"`) that carry their real content inline in `<ac:adf-content>`. Fixed by PR https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/pull/618 (merged).

## Dart status today (verified, not a bug — but not parity either)

The Dart port (`lib/src/integrations/confluence/confluence_markdown.dart`) uses a **structural XML parser** (`_parseXml` → `_storageNodeToMarkdown` → `_wrapStorage`), not the Java regex pipeline. Unknown tags fall through `_wrapInlineStyle`'s default branch which returns children **verbatim**. Consequences:

- ✅ **Synced blocks do NOT lose content** — `ac:adf-extension` / `ac:adf-node` / `ac:adf-content` are all "unknown" and pass their children through, so a `bodied-sync-block`'s inner paragraphs/code/tables survive. The #596 bug does **not** reproduce in Dart.
- ❌ **No `[Diagram]` placeholder for real extensions** — a draw.io/ecosystem extension (`ac:adf-node type="extension"`) currently renders its `ac:adf-attribute` children (extension-key, resource-id GUIDs) as verbatim text noise instead of the clean `[Diagram]` placeholder Java emits.
- ❌ Behavior is **implicit** (relies on the unknown-tag passthrough) and **untested** for both synced blocks and extensions.

## Scope (parity with Java #596)
1. Handle `ac:adf-node` explicitly in `_wrapStorage` (or the block dispatch):
   - `type="bodied-sync-block"` → render the inner `ac:adf-content` content inline (paragraphs, code macros, tables via the existing converters). Today this works by accident via passthrough — make it explicit and lock it with a test.
   - `type="extension"` (draw.io, ecosystem apps — no readable content) → emit the `[Diagram]` placeholder, matching Java.
2. Unit tests in the Dart mirror of the Java `ConfluenceSyncedBlockMarkdownTest`: synced-block paragraph + code macro survive inline (no `[Diagram]`), and a real draw.io extension maps to `[Diagram]` with no attribute GUID leakage.

## Acceptance criteria
- Synced-block content converts inline (same as Java's fixed output).
- Real extensions produce the `[Diagram]` placeholder (Java parity).
- New unit tests cover both cases; existing converter tests stay green.

_Do not assign / implement here — this is a parity tracking issue._

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

```dart
String? _wrapAdfNode(_XmlNode node, String inner) {
  if (node.name != 'ac:adf-node') return null;
  if (node.attrs['type'] != 'bodied-sync-block') return '\n[Diagram]\n';
  final content = node.child('ac:adf-content');
  return content == null ? inner : _storageNodeToMarkdown(content);
}
```

Now let me think about potential issues:

### Issue 1: `ac:adf-extension` wrapper handling

The structure is:
```xml
<ac:adf-extension>
  <ac:adf-node type="bodied-sync-block">
    <ac:adf-attribute key="resource-id">...</ac:adf-attribute>
    <ac:adf-content>...</ac:adf-content>
  </ac:adf-node>
</ac:adf-extension>
```

- `ac:adf-node` → `_wrapAdfNode` handles it.
- `ac:adf-extension` → not handled by any wrapper, falls to `_wrapInlineStyle` default → returns `inner` verbatim. OK.
- `ac:adf-attribute` → falls through to `_wrapInlineStyle` default → returns `inner` (the GUID text) verbatim! But wait — the adf-node handler for synced-block calls `_storageNodeToMarkdown(content)` only on the `ac:adf-content` child, so the attributes of the synced block are skipped — good, no leakage.

But what about a `bodied-sync-block` nested inside... hmm.

### Issue 2: Nested synced blocks / adf-node inside adf-content

If `ac:adf-content` contains a nested `ac:adf-node` (e.g., a synced block containing an extension/diagram), the recursion handles it since `_storageNodeToMarkdown(content)` re-enters the full dispatch chain. OK.

Java parity: what does Java do? Let me check the Java PR #618. Java dm.ai #596/PR 618. In Java, the fix was to render `bodied-sync-block` inline, and keep `[Diagram]` for real extensions. In Dart's `_wrapAdfNode`:

if (node.attrs['type'] != 'bodied-sync-block') return '\n[Diagram]\n';

Let me check what types exist in ADF: `bodied-sync-block`, `extension`, `inlineExtension`, `multiBodiedSyncBlock`, `bodiedExtension`, `blockCard`, `embedCard`... Actually in Confluence storage with `ac:adf-node`, common types include:
- `bodied-sync-block` (synced block)
- `extension` (draw.io etc.)
- `multiBodiedSyncBlock`?

Let me check the Java implementation. The Java repo is https://github.com/epam/dm.ai. Let me search for ConfluenceStorageMarkdown and the PR 618 changes.

### Issue 4: Placement in dispatch chain — `_wrapAdfNode` after `_wrapConfluenceBlock`

`_wrapStorage` chain order: heading/paragraph → list/structural → confluence block → **adf-node** → anchor/image → inline style. Since adf-node is its own tag name, position doesn't conflict with other names. Fine.

If a synced block has `ac:adf-node` with no `type` attribute → treated as extension → `[Diagram]` → content loss? The ticket says the Dart parser passes children through for unknown tags. ```

Not in this ticket's ACs. I could note it as a suggestion at most. Actually wait — let me check if the Dart port handles TOC somewhere else. Let me grep.

**Key parity analysis:**

Java's fallback: `content.find() ? content.group(1) : node` — falls back to the node's RAW inner HTML (which includes the `ac:adf-attribute` GUIDs!). So the Dart fallback `content == null ? inner : ...` mirrors Java's behavior exactly (Java would then convert the raw inner HTML through the pipeline, which — with the generic adf-node rule — would... hmm wait, no. In Java, after unwrapSyncedBlocks replaces the matched adf-node with the raw inner HTML, the remaining `ac:adf-attribute` elements would flow through the pipeline; Java's AC_ADF_NODE rule replaces remaining `<ac:adf-node>...</ac:adf-node>` with [Diagram], but the unwrapped replacement removed those tags. The attributes would leak in Java too. So Dart fallback `inner` (rendered children incl. attribute text) == Java fallback (raw inner HTML incl. attribute text). Parity holds. OK, so the fallback leaking GUIDs is Java-parity — not a deviation. Fine, that downgrades my earlier concern; it's parity-mandated. I might mention it as a nit observation at most. Actually since the PR explicitly documents "mirroring Java's defensive fallback", and the test asserts no GUID leakage for the normal path, this is fine.

**Now the CRITICAL parity question — nested synced blocks and nesting semantics:**

Java uses a lazy regex `(.*?)` with `Pattern.DOTALL` — for NESTED adf-nodes, the lazy match would stop at the FIRST `</ac:adf-node>`, so nested structures break in Java (regex can't nest). Dart's structural parser handles nesting correctly. That's an improvement, not a regression.

But here's a REAL difference: Java's `AC_ADF_SYNC_BLOCK` matches `<ac:adf-node ... type="bodied-sync-block" ...>` — `[^>]*` before and after the type attr. Dart checks `node.attrs['type'] != 'bodied-sync-block'`. Equivalent for well-formed input.

**What about OTHER adf-node types in Java?** The generic rule `AC_ADF_NODE` → `[Diagram]` in Java. Let me check the Java source at main to see the exact generic rule — is it `<ac:adf-node[^>]*>.*?</ac:adf-node>` → `[Diagram]`? If so, Dart's "any non-bodied-sync-block adf-node → [Diagram]" matches Java's generic rule. But also — what about `ac:adf-extension` itself when it directly contains content, or `ac:adf-inline-node`? Let me look at the actual Java file on main.

Let me also check: does Java's generic AC_ADF_NODE rule exist and what does it cover? And does the Dart port handle it identically? In Dart BEFORE this PR: unknown tags passthrough (no [Diagram] at all — the ticket says this is the gap). AFTER this PR: `ac:adf-node` → [Diagram] unless bodied-sync-block. 

But WAIT — what about the WRAPPER `ac:adf-extension`? In the extension test:
```xml
<ac:adf-extension>
  <ac:adf-node type="extension">
    <ac:adf-attribute key="extension-key">drawio</ac:adf-attribute>
  </ac:adf-node>
</ac:adf-extension>
```
The `ac:adf-node` renders `[Diagram]`, and `ac:adf-extension` falls through unknown-tag passthrough → returns children (i.e. `[Diagram]`). Good.

But in the Java pipeline, does the generic adf-node rule ALSO replace `ac:adf-extension`? Let me check the Java main source for `AC_ADF_NODE` and `adf-extension`.

Also check: `ac:adf-attribute` inside an extension that is NOT of type extension... covered.

**What about nested `ac:adf-extension` inside `ac:adf-content` of a synced block containing a diagram?** Nested adf-node type=extension → [Diagram]. Good — recursion handles it; Java regex would break here (lazy match stops at first closing tag — actually in Java the generic rule would also mangle nested ones). Dart is better; no issue.

**Now the ordering issue in `_wrapStorage`:** `_wrapAdfNode` is called AFTER `_wrapConfluenceBlock`. Chain: `_wrapHeadingOrParagraph ?? _wrapListOrStructural ?? _wrapConfluenceBlock ?? _wrapAdfNode ?? _wrapAnchorOrImage ?? _wrapInlineStyle`. Since names are distinct, order among name-dispatched wrappers doesn't matter. OK.

**Edge: `type` attribute missing on a bodied sync block?** ADF spec: bodied sync block has type "bodied-sync-block" — always present. Java requires the type attr to unwrap; Dart requires it too. Parity.

**Edge: attribute value with different quoting/case** — Java uses CASE_INSENSITIVE; the Dart parser lowercases? No — Dart stores attrs as-is. `type="BODIED-SYNC-BLOCK"` would NOT match in Dart; Java would match (CASE_INSENSITIVE). Hyper-theoretical; storage format uses lowercase. Not worth flagging beyond a nit... probably not even worth it.

# dart_test.yaml — configuration for the `dart test` runner.
#
# Test layers (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy, and
# test/integration/README.md):
#
#   L1 unit     — test/**, everything mocked. Default run + CI quality.yml.
#   L2 contract — recorded Java tool traffic replayed against Dart clients.
#   L3 live     — real APIs against sandbox instances; tagged `integration`.
#   L4 agents   — dmtools-agents suite under the Dart runtime (own CI job).
#
# The L3 layer is EXCLUDED from the default run so live-API tests never slow
# down or destabilize the quality loop:
#
#   dart test                                # L1 + L2; the L3 suite is skipped
#
# The `integration` preset opts back in. The default skip is sticky, so
# `-t integration` alone still skips the tag — the preset is what re-enables
# it:
#
#   dart test -P integration -t integration  # L3 only; real credentials needed
#
# CI runs L3 nightly and via workflow_dispatch
# (.github/workflows/integration.yml), never per-PR by default.

tags:
  integration:
    skip: >-
      Live integration test — excluded from the default run. Target a sandbox
      via the DMTOOLS_IT_* variables and run explicitly with
      `dart test -P integration -t integration`.

presets:
  # Re-enables the `integration` tag so the L3 suite can run on demand.
  integration:
    tags:
      integration:
        skip: false

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- Retired the legacy `machine-kit` layer (gh-146): the machine loop runs on
  the factory pack (reusable `agents/.github/workflows/factory/teammate.yml`
  + `sm.yml` behind the thin `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` and
  `machine-sm.yml` stubs). Deleted `machine-kit/teammate-install/`
  (runners/scripts/instructions — superseded by `.dmtools/runners/` +
  `.dmtools/config.js` and the pack's `setup/` scripts),
  `machine-kit/templates/` (superseded by the factory reusable workflows),

  tests repointed to the factory equivalents; runner-wiring contract tests

  submodule pins instead of the `feature/factory-reusable` branch
  (gh-146): the branch head renamed the reusable workflows away from
  `factory/<name>.yml`, so a branch ref would fail every machine trigger
  at run start while the gates stayed green against the submodule copy.

```dart
String? _wrapAdfNode(_XmlNode node, String inner) {
  if (node.name != 'ac:adf-node') return null;
  if (node.attrs['type'] != 'bodied-sync-block') return '\n[Diagram]\n';

One thing: Java's unwrap uses `content.group(1)` — the RAW inner of `ac:adf-content`, then the rest of the pipeline processes it. Dart renders the `ac:adf-content` NODE via `_storageNodeToMarkdown` — the `ac:adf-content` wrapper itself hits `_wrapInlineStyle` default → returns children verbatim. Identical effective behavior. ✅

Another subtlety — Java's AC_ADF_SYNC_BLOCK regex `[^>]*type="bodied-sync-block"[^>]*>`: requires the attribute named `type` with that exact value (case-insensitive). If a bodied-sync-block adf-node carried an `ac:adf-content` ABSENT — fallback. Same. ✅

So an extension inside a table cell → its text content (GUIDs!) would leak into the table cell, since `_collectRows` reads raw `content` and never goes through `_wrapStorage`! Pre-existing behavior for ALL macro-level content in cells (structured-macro inside a td also leaks raw text). blocks.text:
# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

## PR Description

### What changed
Confluence storage→Markdown now handles `ac:adf-node` explicitly (parity with Java dm.ai #596 / PR epam/dm.ai#618): synced blocks (`type="bodied-sync-block"`) render their `<ac:adf-content>` payload inline through the normal converters, while real extensions (draw.io / ecosystem apps) emit the `[Diagram]` placeholder instead of leaking attribute GUID text.

### Key decisions
- Added `_wrapAdfNode` to the `_wrapStorage` dispatch chain (structural parser, so no regex pre-pass like Java's); missing `ac:adf-content` falls back to rendered children, mirroring Java's defensive fallback.
- Split `confluence_markdown.dart` (was 805 lines, over the 800 loc gate) into a `part` file `confluence_markdown_storage.dart` for the storage→Markdown half — repo's existing `part` convention (cf. `jira_client.dart`), zero public API change.
- New `confluence_synced_block_markdown_test.dart` mirrors the Java `ConfluenceSyncedBlockMarkdownTest` (paragraph + code macro survive inline, table converts, no GUID leakage, extension → `[Diagram]`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/integrations/confluence/
crap4dart check --all   # loc gate back under 800; coverage 96.6%
```

# gh-306: Confluence storage→Markdown: adf-node parity — synced blocks inline, real extensions as [Diagram] (Java #596 / PR epam/dm.ai#618)

## Description

## Parity with the Java DMtools (dm.ai) `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown`

Java issue https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/issues/596 fixed a content-loss bug: `<ac:adf-node>` was blanket-replaced with `[Diagram]`, which silently dropped **synced blocks** (`type="bodied-sync-block"`) that carry their real content inline in `<ac:adf-content>`. Fixed by PR https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/pull/618 (merged).

## Dart status today (verified, not a bug — but not parity either)

The Dart port (`lib/src/integrations/confluence/confluence_markdown.dart`) uses a **structural XML parser** (`_parseXml` → `_storageNodeToMarkdown` → `_wrapStorage`), not the Java regex pipeline. Unknown tags fall through `_wrapInlineStyle`'s default branch which returns children **verbatim**. Consequences:

- ✅ **Synced blocks do NOT lose content** — `ac:adf-extension` / `ac:adf-node` / `ac:adf-content` are all "unknown" and pass their children through, so a `bodied-sync-block`'s inner paragraphs/code/tables survive. The #596 bug does **not** reproduce in Dart.
- ❌ **No `[Diagram]` placeholder for real extensions** — a draw.io/ecosystem extension (`ac:adf-node type="extension"`) currently renders its `ac:adf-attribute` children (extension-key, resource-id GUIDs) as verbatim text noise instead of the clean `[Diagram]` placeholder Java emits.
- ❌ Behavior is **implicit** (relies on the unknown-tag passthrough) and **untested** for both synced blocks and extensions.

## Scope (parity with Java #596)
1. Handle `ac:adf-node` explicitly in `_wrapStorage` (or the block dispatch):
   - `type="bodied-sync-block"` → render the inner `ac:adf-content` content inline (paragraphs, code macros, tables via the existing converters). Today this works by accident via passthrough — make it explicit and lock it with a test.
   - `type="extension"` (draw.io, ecosystem apps — no readable content) → emit the `[Diagram]` placeholder, matching Java.
2. Unit tests in the Dart mirror of the Java `ConfluenceSyncedBlockMarkdownTest`: synced-block paragraph + code macro survive inline (no `[Diagram]`), and a real draw.io extension maps to `[Diagram]` with no attribute GUID leakage.

## Acceptance criteria
- Synced-block content converts inline (same as Java's fixed output).
- Real extensions produce the `[Diagram]` placeholder (Java parity).
- New unit tests cover both cases; existing converter tests stay green.

_Do not assign / implement here — this is a parity tracking issue._

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

  if (node.name != 'ac:adf-node') return null;

The structure is:
```xml
<ac:adf-extension>

    <ac:adf-content>...</ac:adf-content>

```

`_wrapStorage` chain order: heading/paragraph → list/structural → confluence block → **adf-node** → anchor/image → inline style. Since adf-node is its own tag name, position doesn't conflict with other names. Fine.

Excellent — I now have the Java PR #618 reference. Key observations:

**Java implementation:**
1. `AC_ADF_SYNC_BLOCK` regex: `<ac:adf-node\b[^>]*type="bodied-sync-block"[^>]*>(.*?)</ac:adf-node>` — matches only `type="bodied-sync-block"`.
2. `AC_ADF_CONTENT`: `<ac:adf-content[^>]*>(.*?)</ac:adf-content>` — inner payload.
3. `unwrapSyncedBlocks`: replaces each matched synced block with the adf-content payload (falling back to the node's raw inner HTML when missing), BEFORE the generic adf-node→[Diagram] rule.
4. The Java code also adds `AC_TOC` removal — `ac:structured-macro ac:name="toc"` → removed as noise! Interesting: the Java PR adds TOC removal as well ("2. Remove table-of-contents macro (auto-generated, adds noise)"). Wait, actually looking at the diff context: `// ac:structured-macro name="toc" (table of contents — auto-generated, noise)` — the AC_TOC pattern appears in the diff hunk as *context or addition*? The hunk `@@ -85,6 +85,19 @@` shows 41 additions with lines:

```
// ac:adf-node type="bodied-sync-block" (synced block) — carries real content
// inline in <ac:adf-content>; must be unwrapped, not dropped (dm.ai #596).
private static final Pattern AC_ADF_SYNC_BLOCK = ...
// inner payload of a synced block
private static final Pattern AC_ADF_CONTENT = ...
// ac:structured-macro name="toc" (table of contents — auto-generated, noise)
private static final Pattern AC_TOC = Pattern.compile(
    "<ac:structured-macro\\s+ac:name=\"toc\"[^>]*/?>",
```

Hmm, the AC_TOC lines might be pre-existing context (the diff table shows them but they may be context lines — hard to tell from the GitHub HTML rendering). The `41 changes: 41 additions & 0 deletions` — the added block spans those lines in the file. The AC_TOC pattern may be pre-existing. Either way, TOC-removal parity isn't in the ticket scope for the Dart port (ticket says Dart already handles toc? let me check). Let me check the Dart `_macroToMarkdown` — no TOC handling. Hmm — is TOC removal in scope? The ticket scope (parity with Java #596) is only synced-block/extension. TOC noise removal is a separate Java behavior (possibly from an earlier Java change). Not in this ticket's ACs. I could note it as a suggestion at most. Actually wait — let me check if the Dart port handles TOC somewhere else. Let me grep.

**Key parity analysis:**

Java's fallback: `content.find() ? content.group(1) : node` — falls back to the node's RAW inner HTML (which includes the `ac:adf-attribute` GUIDs!). So the Dart fallback `content == null ? inner : ...` mirrors Java's behavior exactly (Java would then convert the raw inner HTML through the pipeline, which — with the generic adf-node rule — would... hmm wait, no. In Java, after unwrapSyncedBlocks replaces the matched adf-node with the raw inner HTML, the remaining `ac:adf-attribute` elements would flow through the pipeline; Java's AC_ADF_NODE rule replaces remaining `<ac:adf-node>...</ac:adf-node>` with [Diagram], but the unwrapped replacement removed those tags. The attributes would leak in Java too. So Dart fallback `inner` (rendered children incl. attribute text) == Java fallback (raw inner HTML incl. attribute text). Parity holds. OK, so the fallback leaking GUIDs is Java-parity — not a deviation. Fine, that downgrades my earlier concern; it's parity-mandated. I might mention it as a nit observation at most. Actually since the PR explicitly documents "mirroring Java's defensive fallback", and the test asserts no GUID leakage for the normal path, this is fine.

**Now the CRITICAL parity question — nested synced blocks and nesting semantics:**

Java uses a lazy regex `(.*?)` with `Pattern.DOTALL` — for NESTED adf-nodes, the lazy match would stop at the FIRST `</ac:adf-node>`, so nested structures break in Java (regex can't nest). Dart's structural parser handles nesting correctly. That's an improvement, not a regression.

But here's a REAL difference: Java's `AC_ADF_SYNC_BLOCK` matches `<ac:adf-node ... type="bodied-sync-block" ...>` — `[^>]*` before and after the type attr. Dart checks `node.attrs['type'] != 'bodied-sync-block'`. Equivalent for well-formed input.

**What about OTHER adf-node types in Java?** The generic rule `AC_ADF_NODE` → `[Diagram]` in Java. Let me check the Java source at main to see the exact generic rule — is it `<ac:adf-node[^>]*>.*?</ac:adf-node>` → `[Diagram]`? If so, Dart's "any non-bodied-sync-block adf-node → [Diagram]" matches Java's generic rule. But also — what about `ac:adf-extension` itself when it directly contains content, or `ac:adf-inline-node`? Let me look at the actual Java file on main.

Let me also check: does Java's generic AC_ADF_NODE rule exist and what does it cover? And does the Dart port handle it identically? In Dart BEFORE this PR: unknown tags passthrough (no [Diagram] at all — the ticket says this is the gap). AFTER this PR: `ac:adf-node` → [Diagram] unless bodied-sync-block. 

But WAIT — what about the WRAPPER `ac:adf-extension`? In the extension test:
```xml
<ac:adf-extension>
  <ac:adf-node type="extension">
    <ac:adf-attribute key="extension-key">drawio</ac:adf-attribute>
  </ac:adf-node>
</ac:adf-extension>
```
The `ac:adf-node` renders `[Diagram]`, and `ac:adf-extension` falls through unknown-tag passthrough → returns children (i.e. `[Diagram]`). Good.

But in the Java pipeline, does the generic adf-node rule ALSO replace `ac:adf-extension`? Let me check the Java main source for `AC_ADF_NODE` and `adf-extension`.

Also check: `ac:adf-attribute` inside an extension that is NOT of type extension... covered.

**Another critical check — `ac:adf-content` child that contains block content vs the "content" being rendered via `_storageNodeToMarkdown(content)`:** For a synced block, `content` is `ac:adf-content` node; `_storageNodeToMarkdown` on it → name != null → children rendered → `_wrapStorage('ac:adf-content', parts)` → not heading/list/confluence/adf-node/anchor → `_wrapInlineStyle` → default → `inner` verbatim. 

**What about nested `ac:adf-extension` inside `ac:adf-content` of a synced block containing a diagram?** Nested adf-node type=extension → [Diagram]. Good — recursion handles it; Java regex would break here (lazy match stops at first closing tag — actually in Java the generic rule would also mangle nested ones). Dart is better; no issue.

**Now the ordering issue in `_wrapStorage`:** `_wrapAdfNode` is called AFTER `_wrapConfluenceBlock`. Chain: `_wrapHeadingOrParagraph ?? _wrapListOrStructural ?? _wrapConfluenceBlock ?? _wrapAdfNode ?? _wrapAnchorOrImage ?? _wrapInlineStyle`. Since names are distinct, order among name-dispatched wrappers doesn't matter. OK.

**Edge: `type` attribute missing on a bodied sync block?** ADF spec: bodied sync block has type "bodied-sync-block" — always present. Java requires the type attr to unwrap; Dart requires it too. Parity.

**Edge: attribute value with different quoting/case** — Java uses CASE_INSENSITIVE; the Dart parser lowercases? No — Dart stores attrs as-is. `type="BODIED-SYNC-BLOCK"` would NOT match in Dart; Java would match (CASE_INSENSITIVE). Hyper-theoretical; storage format uses lowercase. Not worth flagging beyond a nit... probably not even worth it.

**Now, the `inlineExtension`/`ac:adf-inline-node` case:** `type="inlineExtension"` nodes → `[Diagram]\n` with newlines. Java generic rule likely produces `[Diagram]` similarly inline. Fine.

Let me now check the Java main file for the generic rule to be thorough. The clone failed (repo `dm.ai.java` doesn't exist — the repo is `dm.ai`). Let me clone the right repo.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.
